key_insight: Neural Eigenfluid Bases learn spatially continuous, ordered flow modes that enforce incompressibility and impermeable boundaries while supporting compact reduced-order simulation.
engineering_relevance: Reusing a learned basis with precomputed Galerkin operators enables millisecond-scale updates and a reduced state about 1,000 times smaller than the full reference model.
method: Enforce physical constraints through differential lifts and potential boundary conditions.
Learn ordered modes using geometry-local orthogonalization and Rayleigh minimization, with gauge fixing to reduce derivative requirements.
Learn independent circulation fields around obstacles using a Dirichlet energy loss.
evidence_signal: With 1,024 modes, both learning objectives keep periodic vortex-merger velocity errors below 1%; potential-based learning also captures more initial energy and yields lower final errors than same-size numerical Laplacian bases for random obstacle flows.
watch_item: Millisecond-scale updates depend on basis reuse and precomputed operators; coefficient-evolution errors remain distinct from spatial reconstruction errors.
paper_title: Neural Eigenfluid Bases: Spectral Objectives, Gauge, and Topology
